> *"XLK closed the week at $183.23, down 0.13%, which hides a 3.3% Thursday that took it to $182.34, under last Friday's low close. Lam Research reported a record quarter Wednesday night (revenue $8.22B, +54% y/y, a 40.2% operating margin) and fell 11.8% Thursday on a December guide of $8.6B ±$400M that the market read as a ceiling; AMAT fell 8.2% in sympathy. AAPL set a two-year closing high of $348.22 Thursday and PLTR rose 5.8%. The 10-year closed under 5.00% Thursday and Friday for the first time since Sep 22, October hike odds collapsed to under 10%, and the fund still could not hold its 50D. VIX 19.45."*

**Marky Tape Read:** A flat week that was not flat. **Monday** gapped up to $186.99 and closed $185.96 on 9.1M — the Arena ingest booked this fund's open as a rejected print (open above the bar's high), so take the open with care. **Tuesday** dipped to $182.81 and recovered to $185.44. **Wednesday** rallied to $188.54, a high of $189.11, under the 50D ($189.53) by 42 cents — the second failed test of the 50D in two weeks. **Thursday** -3.3% to $182.34 on 12.1M, the low $181.50, a new low close for the move, under last Friday's $182.82 intraday low. **Friday** +0.5% to **$183.23** on 7.4M, the lightest volume of the week; the bounce had no sponsorship. RSI 38.2 from 33.4. 20D $193.23 falling, 50D $189.53 flat, 200D $168.19 rising. Range for the week $181.50 – $189.11; the fund closed in the lower third of it.

**Ophelia Macro Read:** The bond market gave tech everything it asked for and tech did nothing with it. The 10Y (Treasury par) closed **4.96% Thursday and 5.00% Friday**, from 5.09%; Yahoo ^TNX printed 4.95 and 4.99, its first closes under 5.00 since Sep 22. The 30Y fell to **5.33%** from 5.43%. The 2Y fell to **4.69%** from 4.74%, so **2s10s narrowed to +31bp** from +35 — a bull flattening for a second week. October hike odds, which were 42–52% a week ago, are now **about 7–8%** (CME-based trackers quoted Oct 23); a December hike is still priced as more likely than not on one account (80.5% by Dec 9, CME via BeInCrypto). The dollar read **101.75 Fri evening** (DX-Y.NYB), flat. **WTI read $103.44 Fri evening (CL=F, last trade)** against last week's $101.41 settlement (CLX26, market_state.json); Brent **$111.66 Fri evening**, above $111 Thursday on Iran war worries (Yahoo). Gold read **$4,010 Fri evening** (GC=F), down from the $4,159.50 settlement — its lowest close since Jul 16 on the continuous read. VIX **19.45**, after 16.68 Wednesday. SPY -0.43%. The gates are **MSFT and the FOMC on Oct 28, INTC Oct 29, AAPL and PLTR Nov 2**.

Targets = Yahoo mean (pulled Oct 23); **LRCX's mean target was cut from $375.81 to $364.03** after the print — the only target that moved more than a dollar. Weights = State Street via Yahoo funds_data (Oct 23 pull) — **identical to the two prior weeks to the basis point**; Yahoo is not refreshing them and no new name entered the top ten. AMAT (#11) **$377.24 (-7.8%)**, mean target $627.83. ORCL $126.16 (-1.6%). SMH $527.20 (-2.3%), lowest close since Jul 29.

**Concentration Risk:** Top 3 = 39.7% and top 10 = 64.5% on the stale weights. AAPL has risen two weeks running while the chips fell; its live weight is above 13.6%.

**The week's split:** **Eight of the ten fell**, two rose. The casualty was **LRCX -12.8%**: a record September quarter — revenue **$8.22B (+54% y/y)**, adjusted EPS **$2.20** against a $2.18 consensus, gross margin 52.4%, a record **40.2% operating margin** — and a December guide of **$8.6B ±$400M** that was read as capped by supply constraints and a sharp expected drop in China revenue (Yahoo/MarketBeat/Bernstein, Oct 21–22). The stock fell **11.8% Thursday** on 23.0M shares to $230.15 and did not bounce Friday; the $230.10 close is its lowest since Apr 6. **AMAT -7.8%** followed it (-8.2% Thursday). **INTC -3.2%** to $86.96 ahead of its Oct 29 print, now 38% off its 52-week high close; no company news found. **PLTR +5.8%** recovered half of the prior week's loss with no Palantir-specific headline found. **AAPL +1.2%**, a two-year closing high of **$348.22 Thursday** — the day the rest of the fund fell 3.3%. NVDA -1.5%, MSFT -0.9%, MU -0.1% were the quiet ones.

**Cecil Fundamental Read:** Lam gave me exactly the print I said I would wait for and the stock fell 12% anyway. Record revenue, record margins, a guide above the quarter just reported — and the Street cut its target because the guide was not higher. At $230.10 the stock is 18.9x forward with a 58% gap to the mean target. That gap is now wide enough that either the analysts are wrong or the price is, and I am paid to find out which. **I start a position in LRCX here** — small, a third of what I would want, because the tape has not stopped falling and I was wrong about MU for the same reason two weeks ago. MSFT at 22.1x forward, down 0.9% in a week the chips broke again, reports Wednesday and remains the core add. MU at 4.2x forward I hold and do not add. AAPL at 36x and 5.6% above its mean target I still do not follow.

## THE WEEKLY NARRATIVE — What's Actually Moving XLK

> *This section is rewritten weekly by the Saturday Research Crew. It captures the story beneath the headlines.*

### This Week's Story: Good Numbers, Bad Reactions

XLK closed **$183.23, -0.13%**, after trading from $189.11 down to $181.50. SMH lost 2.3% to its lowest close since Jul 29. The S&P 500 fell 0.47% and the Nasdaq Composite 0.71%.

**Catalyst 1 — Lam beats and falls (Wed Oct 21, after the close):** Revenue $8.22B, up 54%; EPS $2.20 against $2.18; a record 40.2% operating margin. The December guide, $8.6B ±$400M, was above the quarter just reported. Accounts cite a wide range, supply limits on the guide, lower China revenue and an 80% one-year run (Yahoo, BigGo, Benzinga). LRCX fell 11.8% Thursday and AMAT 8.2%. Bernstein called the quarter slightly better than expected and still sees 2027 wafer-fab spending of at least $200B.

**Catalyst 2 — Meta spends more (Wed Oct 21):** Meta beat on revenue and raised its capex forecast. The stock fell about 7% Thursday. Coverage tied Thursday's chip selloff to renewed doubt about AI returns. SMH closed down 6.0% that day (about 3.4% at midday, per same-day coverage), and chips and AI made up 93% of the Nasdaq-100's morning loss (StockTitan).

**Catalyst 3 — The Fed exits the story:** October hike odds fell from about half to under 10%. The 10Y closed under 5.00% for the first time since Sep 22. Tech got the rate relief it wanted and still fell Thursday.

**Catalyst 4 — Oil:** Brent traded above $111 Thursday on Iran war worries (Yahoo). WTI read $103.44 Friday evening against a $101.41 settlement.

**The exceptions:** AAPL closed at a two-year high Thursday, the day the fund fell 3.3%. PLTR rose 5.8%.

**The Bottom Line:** Two weeks ago the problem was rates. This week rates eased and the problem became the bill for the buildout. Next week the people paying it — MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN — report alongside the FOMC.

## RISK SCENARIOS

### 🟢 Bull Case
- MSFT (Oct 28) holds its capex plan and the stock rises; the chain gets a buyer again
- The Fed holds as priced, the 10Y stays under 5.0%, and XLK closes over the 50D ($189.53)
- The double low at $181.50–$181.55 holds and LRCX's 58% gap to its mean target starts to close

### 🔴 Bear Case
- A close under **$181.50** confirms the break; next support $172.50, then the 200D at $168.19
- Hyperscalers cut or hold capex next week and the supplier selloff deepens
- INTC (Oct 29) misses into a three-week -27% slide
- AAPL, at a two-year high and 36x forward, gives way — it has been the fund's support for two weeks

### ⚠️ The Wild Card
**Good news is being sold.** Lam beat on revenue, EPS and margin and fell 12%. Meta beat on revenue and fell 7%. The Fed's October hike went from a coin flip to under 10% and the fund still fell 3.3% on Thursday. If MSFT and Alphabet beat next week and are sold the same way, the problem is the sector's multiple, not its earnings, and the 200D becomes the target.

### This Week's Story: The Buyer Held, the Toolmaker Slipped, the Sector Fell Anyway

Last week the question was whether anyone downstream could pay. This week a buyer answered yes, and a supplier said it could not ship fast enough. The market sold both answers.

**Act I — The Bounce.** Monday SOX snapped its eight-day losing streak, the longest since 2008, and SMH rose 1.6% to $548.46. China's Q3 GDP printed 4.5% against 4.4%, export-led. Tuesday housing starts came in at 1.221M against 1.30M, and builder sentiment fell to 29. SMH drifted. **Act II — The Reports.** After Wednesday's close: Lam set a record and said supply constraints held back its guide. Meta narrowed its capex range upward and gave no 2027 number. TI beat. LRCX -11.8%, AMAT -8.2%, KLAC ~-10%, AMD -8.1%, ARM -7.3%, ASML -6.9%, NVDA -4.4%, Meta -7.0%, CoreWeave -10.1%. **SOX -6.72%, all 30 members down, about $200B erased (TechTimes).** SMH -5.99% to $523.35 on 15.3M shares. **The Bottom Line.** The demand data held: Meta's budget, Lam's record and visibility through 2028, TrendForce raising its Q4 DRAM call to ~+20%.
